title: Jonah and the Lantern
premise: In 1890s pearling port of Ceylon's northern coast, Freya Halloran discovers that the handwriting on a stranger's letters belongs to her father — declared drowned five years ago, the same year the Halloran Trading Company's ledgers began hiding deaths at sea. The stranger, a disgraced company clerk named Elias Voss, carries proof that the company's founder has been falsifying drownings to claim insurance and silence divers who knew too much. As Freya gathers testimony from the diving community she was taught to distrust, she must choose between the safety of silence and the peril of record, racing to deposit sworn statements with a colonial magistrate before the company's hired men destroy both the evidence and its keepers. The book ends with the truth entered into the public record, the founder's empire collapsing, and Freya — no longer indentured, no longer silent — choosing to stay with the found family that testified beside her.
about_author: Zephyrine Winterbourne is the pen name of a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloguing colonial shipping records before turning to fiction. She writes from a coastal cottage where, she insists, every drawer contains at least one unfinished letter.

chapters.title: The Weight of Water
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. We meet seventeen-year-old Freya sorting pearls by lamplight in the Halloran compound, establishing the silences she's learned: never look at ledgers, never name the drowned. When a diver's widow is turned away unpaid, Freya quietly slips her bread — a small act of defiance that costs her a beating. Emotional beat: the ache of belonging nowhere.

chapters.title: A Stranger with Familiar Ink
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Elias Voss arrives at the trading post seeking the daughter of 'drowned' diver Tomas Halloran, carrying letters in Tomas's unmistakable hand dated after his death. Freya recognizes the writing that once covered her childhood lessons. She denies knowing him — then follows him into the rain. Emotional beat: vertigo; the ground of her whole life shifting.

chapters.title: What the Ledgers Keep
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. In a fisherman's hut, Elias reveals he kept the company's true books: forty-one men recorded as lost at sea whose debts were collected anyway, their insurance payouts pocketed by founder Augustus Halloran. Tomas may be alive, imprisoned on a remote curing station. Freya refuses to believe it until Elias shows her her father's private mark on each page. Emotional beat: grief colliding with furious hope.

chapters.title: The Divers' Tongue
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Freya begins secretly canvassing widows and retired divers, discovering they've shared suspicions for years in a coded pidgin the company never bothered to learn. Old diver Sefu becomes her first ally, teaching her that silence protected no one — it only decided who got hurt. Emotional beat: the first warmth of found family.

chapters.title: An Audience with the Founder
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Summoned before Augustus Halloran, Freya performs the perfect obedient ward while probing what he knows. He offers her freedom papers if she'll report on 'agitators' among the divers — revealing he already suspects something. She accepts, becoming a double agent in her own home. Emotional beat: power's seduction and rot, tasted firsthand.

chapters.title: Fire on the Cure Station Road
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Elias rides to verify Tomas's location but is ambushed by company men; wounded, he barely escapes as they burn the station's records ahead of any inquiry. He realizes Augustus is destroying evidence faster than they can gather it. Meanwhile Freya covers his absence with a forged ledger entry — her first outright crime. Emotional beat: terror hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: Sworn on Salt Water
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. In a midnight gathering aboard a beached boat, eleven witnesses give their accounts before Magistrate's clerk Ruth Adeyemi, a sympathetic outsider who agrees to hold depositions. The community that silence once divided binds itself together in testimony. But one attendee slips away early — a traitor among them. Emotional beat: belonging earned, and immediately endangered.

chapters.title: The Price of Names
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Augustus confronts Freya with the traitor's report, offering her everything — freedom, wealth, even a search for her father — if she recants and names the others. She looks at the man who raised her profit off the drowned and refuses. Arrests begin; Sefu is taken. Emotional beat: the cost of power refused, paid in people she loves.

chapters.title: Jonah and the Lantern
chapters.summary: Alternating POV climax. During a storm, Freya and Elias break Sefu from the company lockup and race the deposition trunk to the magistrate's court as Augustus's men close in. Freya testifies while floodwater rises through the courthouse floor, her voice steady over the storm — the silence finally broken on the record. Augustus arrives too late; the depositions are sealed. Emotional beat: triumph carved out of desperation.

chapters.title: What the Tide Returns
chapters.summary: Freya's POV, months later. The company collapses under investigation; word comes that Tomas Halloran was indeed alive and freed when the station fell — and that he is coming home. Freya, her indenture voided, stands on the shore with Sefu, Ruth, and Elias, deciding not whether to belong, but to whom. She lights the harbor lantern herself. Emotional beat: quiet, chosen joy.
